Field guide / 01—08

Measure a rectangular room

Record the right length and width for the surface you intend to cover.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Start with the surface you will work on

For a rectangular floor, measure the inside edges of the area to be covered. Record length and width in metres, along with the date and raw measurements. If opposite sides differ, check the actual shape before relying on a single rectangle.

Calculate with units

Floor area = length × width. Two lengths in metres produce square metres (m²), not metres. Convert 320 cm to 3.20 m before multiplying it by a measurement in metres. For a wall, use wall width × wall height and record openings separately.

Check the site again

A small labelled sketch makes swapped dimensions easier to spot. Measure uneven edges at several points. A calculator only uses the numbers entered; the actual shape, gaps and obstacles still need an on-site check.

Worked example

A 4.20 m × 3.50 m floor has an area of 14.70 m². This is its base area; the tile order may increase with cuts and the allowance you choose.

Pitfall to avoid

Do not multiply 420 cm by 3.50 m. Convert to consistent units first or the result will be 100 times too large.
